current.text: He picked up his 5 million USD player option and stays in Milwaukee. The experts read this as a sign that no other team wanted him.
He missed most of last season.
Doc Rivers is no longer the Milwaukee coach. Porter played big minutes under Rivers as his preferred player. The new coach is Taylor Jenkins.
The Milwaukee backcourt is crowded with Rollins, Herro, Jakucionis, Burries, Trent and Green. The projected starters are Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Turner.
The experts expect him to come off the bench, with minutes well below last season. Josh thinks Ryan Rollins starts over him, and he could play about 27 minutes as a reserve.
Justin thinks his best role is as a sixth man scorer leading the second unit.
He is worth a late pick, around 120 but not earlier. He is a flyer in case Milwaukee starts him, and Josh calls him a must-draft at that point.
His 2.2 steals per game last season are the steals number most likely to drop a lot, because he was not a big steals player before.

durable.text: Steals are his standout category, well above the top 250 pool.
He makes few threes for a guard. His three-point attempts disappeared in Milwaukee.
His scoring efficiency relies on tough mid-range shots, and Justin thinks that is unlikely to last.
His FT% is hard to predict. He has a 60% season in his career and also seasons near 77% and 88%.
The experts do not rate him as a real-life player. One calls him inefficient and a ball hog, though the fantasy numbers are strong when he plays big minutes.

note: He is an end-of-auction flyer for us. Yahoo and ESPN value him at 2 to 3 USD, and our league paid 3 USD last season. His ranks (107 ESPN, 158 Yahoo) put him near the edge of our 144-player pool, so do not pay more than 1 to 3 USD. He fits punt 3PM builds that want steals and assists from a guard. Early in the season, check whether he starts or gets 27 or more minutes under Jenkins, and whether his steals stay near 2 per game. If neither happens, he is easy to drop.
